proposals: IRDAI should publish each year the reinsurance premium ceded by Indian insurers, split between the obligatory cession to GIC Re, other domestic reinsurers, GIFT City branches and cross-border reinsurers, so whether the float is being kept onshore can be read from outcomes, not licence counts.

The General Insurance Council should publish restated segment-wise comparatives on a consistent basis after the October 2024 change excluding long-term premium, so readers do not mistake 6.2% headline growth for 8.6% underlying growth, segment by segment as well as in total.

The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways and IRDAI should publish, each year and by state and vehicle type, the share of registered vehicles holding valid third-party cover, so the uninsured gap, which this post found no estimate reliable enough to quote, is measured officially.

IRDAI should publish industry-wide claims-development data for motor third-party business, including the average time from accident to Motor Accident Claims Tribunal settlement, so the length of the long tail that generates float is a published figure rather than a range.

IRDAI should publish quarterly industry totals of general and life insurers' holdings by Category of Investments bucket, A to E, so the share of insurance float that actually reaches the equity market can be tracked without reading every insurer's returns.
